note: Reflection prompts are editorial applications of the cited passages, not Bible quotations or a validated diagnostic instrument. Review interpretations with your church. The full bank is retained for optional deeper reflection.

formMetadata.title: Spiritual Gifts Discovery
formMetadata.introText: Explore how you may serve others through the gifts God gives. Reflect honestly on your experience, then consider your results with Scripture, prayer, and people who know you.

completionMessage.heading: Thank you!
completionMessage.body: Pray about your results and talk with a leader you trust.

highAgreementNotice.text: Many areas have high scores. These scores may not distinguish your gifts clearly; reflect on concrete examples with someone who knows you.

nextSteps: Read the passages connected to your results in their wider context.
Ask someone who knows you how they have seen you serve others.
Try a practical opportunity to serve with your church and reflect on its fruit.
Let love guide how you use every gift (1 Corinthians 13:1–3).
results.disclaimer: This reflection does not determine what the Holy Spirit has given you or confer a ministry office. Gifts are given for the good of others, as the Spirit wills (1 Corinthians 12:7–11). Explore your results through Scripture, prayer, service, and your church community.

love.heading: Above all, love
love.body: Whatever gifts you explore, use them in love. Paul teaches that even remarkable gifts and generous acts gain us nothing without love (1 Corinthians 13:1–3). Among faith, hope, and love, the greatest is love.

quotes.text: But the greatest of these is love.

groups.title: Gifts of the Spirit
groups.subtitle: The gifts listed in 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12
groups.intro: Reflect on gifts and service named in 1 Corinthians 12 and Romans 12. The Spirit gives gifts for the good of others. These questions explore your experience; they do not determine what God has given or appoint you to an office. Some statements describe experiences you have; others describe difficulties or experiences you have not had. Read each one carefully. There is no preferred answer. Limited opportunity to serve can affect your responses; this is not a measure of your faith.

categories.name: Wisdom
categories.description: Knowing what to do in a hard situation, and how God’s Word applies to it.

items.text: I help a group consider wise choices when a decision is difficult.
People come to me when they have a hard decision to make.
I can help people think through a difficult situation in light of Scripture.
People have told me that my advice helped them make a wise decision.
I find it difficult to connect a biblical truth with a practical decision someone faces.
I help people consider the likely consequences of a decision.
I have helped someone through a big life decision using God’s Word.
I can see a way forward when other people feel lost.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Knowledge
categories.description: Sharing understanding of God’s truth for the good of others.

items.text: I have shared an insight I believed God had given, and others helped test whether it was true.
Prayer and study have helped me understand something that I could share for others’ benefit.
I have shared an insight about God’s truth that helped someone understand their situation.
I seek to understand God’s truth so I can help others.
I find it difficult to put an insight about God’s truth into words that help someone understand.
Mature believers have helped confirm the truth of an insight I shared.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: 1 Corinthians 12 names a word or message of knowledge without describing a questionnaire test for it. These prompts explore sharing understanding for others’ good; Christians differ on how this gift operates.

categories.name: Faith
categories.description: A deep, steady trust that God will act, which lifts the faith of others.

items.text: I stay sure that God can act, even when things look impossible.
I find it difficult to help others trust God when their circumstances seem hopeless.
I have taken a step for God where I had to depend on Him completely.
I see ways to serve God where other people only see problems.
I encourage a discouraged group to keep trusting God.
When I speak about God’s promises, other people’s faith grows.
I have continued to trust God while waiting for an answer to prayer.
I have acted in faith after considering Scripture and wise counsel.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Healings
categories.description: Serving others through prayer for healing, depending on God for the outcome.

items.text: Praying with people who are ill is rarely part of my experience of serving others.
I often feel prompted to pray for someone who is ill.
People have told me they got better after I prayed with them.
When I have the opportunity, I pray with people who are ill.
I trust God as I pray for people who are ill, without promising a particular outcome.
I keep praying for the sick even when I do not see results yet.
I check on people I have prayed for to see how they are doing.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: God gives gifts of healings as He wills (1 Corinthians 12:9–11). An answer to this questionnaire cannot verify a healing or guarantee an outcome.

categories.name: Miracles
categories.description: Reflecting on remarkable works of God associated with prayer and service.

items.text: I have witnessed an unusual answer to prayer that I understood as God’s work.
I have witnessed an answer to prayer that I understood as a remarkable act of God.
I pray boldly when a situation needs God to do something impossible.
I give God the credit when I see remarkable answers to prayer.
I have seen God step in, in a surprising and powerful way.
I have little experience of others describing an answer to prayer with me as a remarkable act of God.
I am comfortable praying for big breakthroughs.
I pray with confidence in God’s power while leaving the outcome to Him.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: 1 Corinthians 12:10 names the working of miracles. These answers describe reported experiences; they do not verify a miracle or establish its cause.

categories.name: Prophecy
categories.description: Sharing a message from God that builds up, encourages, or comforts people.

items.text: I sometimes feel prompted to share a message that I believe may be from God.
During prayer or worship, I sometimes have a message to share for others to weigh.
I have little experience of sharing a message I believed was from God for others to weigh.
Messages I share help strengthen, encourage, or comfort others in their faith.
Other believers have weighed a message I shared and found it consistent with Scripture and helpful.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: Messages should build up others and be weighed by the church (1 Corinthians 14:3, 29). A score does not establish that a message comes from God.

categories.name: Discerning of Spirits
categories.description: Weighing spiritual claims and distinguishing truth from error.

items.text: I carefully consider whether a spiritual message agrees with Scripture.
I weigh spiritual claims carefully rather than assuming every strong feeling comes from God.
I notice when a teaching conflicts with Scripture.
I check a spiritual concern against Scripture and seek wise counsel before drawing conclusions.
I find it difficult to explain why a spiritual claim conflicts with Scripture.
I seek to distinguish truth from error when people make spiritual claims.
Others ask me to help them weigh spiritual claims against Scripture.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These prompts explore careful discernment; a feeling or suspicion alone does not establish a spiritual cause (1 John 4:1).

categories.name: Tongues
categories.description: Speaking or praying in tongues, with public use guided by the order described in 1 Corinthians 14.

items.text: Speaking in tongues is not part of my experience.
I pray in tongues several times a week.
In prayer or worship, I feel a pull to pray in tongues.
Praying in tongues makes me stronger in spirit and closer to God.
I sometimes pray in tongues for other people or situations.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Interpretation of Tongues
categories.description: Understanding and explaining what is spoken in tongues, so that everyone is built up.

items.text: When someone speaks in tongues in a meeting, I sometimes get a sense of what it means.
I have received words or pictures in my mind that seemed to explain a message in tongues.
I have little experience of sharing an interpretation of tongues in a gathering.
People have told me my interpretation helped or encouraged them.
When tongues are spoken in a meeting, I listen closely for the meaning.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Service / Helps
categories.description: Doing practical work that makes it possible for others to do ministry.

items.text: I enjoy practical work that helps others do ministry well.
I willingly do practical work that supports the church’s shared life.
I notice practical needs and look for ways to help.
When I see a job nobody has been given, I do it without being asked.
I feel happy when I help people get God’s work done.
People rarely turn to me for help with practical ministry tasks.
I enjoy behind-the-scenes work that supports leaders and events.
I tend to avoid routine practical tasks when help is needed.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Teaching
categories.description: Explaining God’s Word clearly so people understand and grow.

items.text: I give time to preparing Bible lessons carefully.
I find it difficult to explain Bible passages in a way others understand.
People often ask me to explain hard Bible passages.
I enjoy preparing lessons, Bible studies, or teaching materials.
I can tell the difference between true Bible teaching and wrong teaching.
It really bothers me when people misunderstand an important Bible teaching.
I check carefully that what I teach is correct and based on Scripture.
I enjoy helping a group understand a Bible passage.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Encouragement
categories.description: Encouraging, motivating, and urging people forward in their faith.

items.text: People rarely seek me out for encouragement when they are struggling to keep going.
I can correct someone gently and still leave them encouraged.
I help people consider a practical step forward in their faith.
I move people to act on what the Bible says.
I can lift up someone who is discouraged, confused, or weak in faith.
I see the best in people and help them see it too.
I am drawn to people who need someone to believe in them.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Giving
categories.description: Giving money and resources freely and cheerfully for God’s work.

items.text: I willingly share my resources to help others.
I notice needs that could be met by sharing resources.
I feel great joy when my money or things help God’s work.
Sharing resources to meet a need, within what I can afford, is rarely part of my experience of serving.
I pray about how to use my money to do the most good for God’s kingdom.
I feel blessed when I can meet someone’s need by giving.
It is hard for me to give money away.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Leadership
categories.description: Guiding people toward a goal and helping others grow as leaders.

items.text: Others ask me to help guide a shared task.
I enjoy getting people to work together toward one goal.
I find it difficult to help a group agree on a direction for its ministry.
I listen to others before making a difficult decision for the group.
I help a group agree on a direction when its next step is unclear.
I enjoy training other leaders instead of keeping all the work to myself.
I am willing to take responsibility when a group needs guidance.
I can inspire others to follow a vision.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: Romans 12:8 names leading; 1 Corinthians 12:28 names administrations. These related categories may overlap.

categories.name: Administration
categories.description: Planning, organizing, and making things run well.

items.text: I find it difficult to turn a ministry goal into a workable plan.
I notice when important details have been missed.
I enjoy planning events, schedules, and activities.
I keep track of tasks so important work is completed.
I help organize ministry work when plans are unclear.
I like to see things done properly and with attention to detail.
I can see how to make a process faster or simpler.
I often leave important planning details unfinished.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: Planning is a practical application of administrations in 1 Corinthians 12:28, not a complete biblical definition of the gift.

categories.name: Mercy
categories.description: Caring for people who are hurting, with kindness you can see.

items.text: I feel the pain of other people deeply, even people I barely know.
I am drawn to people who are hurting, rejected, or forgotten.
Spending time caring for people going through hard times is rarely part of my experience of serving.
I stay kind to someone even after they have failed again and again.
I am happy to spend a lot of time listening to hurting people.
I notice when people need emotional support.
I have made time to care for someone who was hurting, even when it was inconvenient.
It is hard for me to listen to people’s problems for a long time.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: These reflection prompts apply the cited passage to everyday service; they are not a biblical test for possessing a gift.

categories.name: Pioneering gospel service (apostolic)
categories.description: Exploring pioneering gospel service and helping establish communities of believers.

items.text: I want to help establish communities where people can learn to follow Jesus.
I am willing to help begin gospel ministry where there are few Christians.
I can help plan how a new gospel ministry might begin.
I have little experience of helping start a group that shares the gospel and supports believers.
I am willing to help establish new ministry while valuing existing churches.
I am comfortable going to unfamiliar places for the sake of the gospel.
I care deeply about God’s work growing beyond my own church.
I pray about opportunities to share the gospel in new places.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: 1 Corinthians 12:28 names apostles. These prompts explore pioneering gospel service, not apostolic office or authority. Christians differ on the present-day application of this role.

sharedTraits.name: Strengthening others through words
sharedTraits.interpretationNote: Paul connects intelligible contributions with building up the church; Judas and Silas illustrate prophetic encouragement. Applying this shared purpose to these prompts is interpretive.

items.text: People have told me that something I shared helped them continue following Christ during a difficult time.
I find it difficult to offer words that help a discouraged believer keep going.

sharedTraits.name: Helping others understand and apply truth
sharedTraits.interpretationNote: Teaching with wisdom is explicit; connecting understanding and evaluation with knowledge and discernment is an editorial application, not an exhaustive definition of those gifts.

items.text: I have helped someone understand how a biblical truth relates to a situation they faced.
I find it difficult to help someone examine a confusing spiritual claim in light of Scripture.

sharedTraits.name: Coordinating practical service
sharedTraits.interpretationNote: Acts describes a response to overlooked needs through shared responsibility. These modern category connections are inferred from the narrative, not gift labels assigned by Luke.

items.text: I find it difficult to help a group agree on who will carry out a shared task.
I have helped a group put a practical plan into action so that people were better served.

sharedTraits.name: Meeting concrete needs
sharedTraits.interpretationNote: Tabitha’s practical care illustrates overlap in service, generosity and mercy; Acts does not name her particular gifts.

items.text: When someone is struggling, I look for a practical way to help with what they need.
I have little experience of making time or sharing resources to help someone whose needs were overlooked.

sharedTraits.name: Praying with people in difficult circumstances
sharedTraits.interpretationNote: These passages connect prayer, trust and requests for healing or signs. Prayer is for all believers and cannot establish a healing, miracle or a particular gift.

items.text: When people face circumstances they cannot change, I join them in asking God for help.
Praying alongside someone through an ongoing difficulty is rarely part of my experience.

sharedTraits.name: Helping others begin and grow in service
sharedTraits.interpretationNote: Equipping is a shared purpose of the ministries in Ephesians. Its application to pioneering service and Romans 12 leadership is interpretive and does not establish an office.

items.text: I have helped another believer prepare to take responsibility for serving others.
I find it difficult to guide someone through their first steps in a ministry.

groups.title: Ways to serve
groups.subtitle: Optional reflection on ministry and biblical practices
groups.intro: Explore ways to serve described across Scripture. Evangelists and pastors are named in Ephesians 4:11. Other categories are biblical practices or examples, not additional gifts explicitly listed in 1 Corinthians 12 or Romans 12.

categories.name: Evangelism
categories.description: Sharing the good news so that people come to know Jesus.

items.text: I enjoy talking with non-believers about Jesus.
I look for chances to share the gospel.
I can explain the gospel clearly to someone who is not a Christian.
When I have the opportunity, I start conversations about Jesus with people outside the church.
I am comfortable starting spiritual talks with strangers.
I have led someone to Christ or helped them take a step closer to Jesus.
I look for respectful ways to talk about Jesus in everyday conversation.
I avoid talking about Jesus with people outside the church.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Pastoring / Shepherding
categories.description: Caring for people’s spiritual growth over the long term.

items.text: I remember people’s spiritual needs and pray for them during the week.
I follow up on people who are missing, struggling, or weak in faith.
People trust me with their personal and spiritual problems.
I enjoy helping new believers get started and then grow over a long time.
I am patient as I walk with people through their growth.
I feel responsible for helping people become strong in Christ.
I keep real friendships with the people I care for spiritually.
I make time to support someone who is struggling in faith.

categories.basis: Named in the gift or ministry lists
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Missionary / Cross-Cultural
categories.description: Taking the gospel to other cultures and people groups.

items.text: I care deeply about people and communities outside my normal world.
I would change the way I live to serve people from another culture.
I want to take the gospel to places where Jesus is less known.
I am willing to learn from people whose culture differs from mine.
I have taken real steps toward serving in another culture or region, like learning a language or asking questions about it.
I enjoy making friends across tribe, culture, or social background.
I have taken part in missions or cross-cultural ministry.
I am willing to explore serving Christ among people of another culture.

categories.basis: Biblical practice of service
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Hospitality
categories.description: Welcoming people and making them feel at home.

items.text: I enjoy welcoming people into my home or church.
Visitors often feel at ease around me.
I notice when someone is left out or feels unwelcome.
I enjoy preparing food or creating a place where people can relax and share life together.
I especially enjoy welcoming newcomers, strangers, and guests.
I make space in my life to welcome people who need friendship.
I willingly welcome people even when hosting takes effort.
I make people feel at home and cared for.

categories.basis: Biblical practice of service
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Intercession
categories.description: Praying faithfully for other people and the church.

items.text: I regularly return to prayer for particular people or situations.
I keep praying even when I see no answer yet.
I often become aware of people or situations that need prayer.
I set aside time to pray for others without being reminded.
I continue to pray for others and thank God for answers to prayer.
Praying for others is a regular part of how I serve.
I regularly pray for decisions that affect my church community.
I find it difficult to keep praying for others consistently.

categories.basis: Biblical practice of service
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Worship / Music
categories.description: Helping others worship God through singing and music.

items.text: I naturally show my love for God through music or singing.
I help others worship God through singing or music.
Singing helps me reflect on God’s truth with gratitude.
People have asked me to lead or play music for worship.
I practise music or worship skills on my own time, without being asked.
I help others focus on God’s truth through music.
Music is a big part of how I live out and show my faith.
I enjoy joining others in songs that honor God.

categories.basis: Biblical practice of service
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Craftsmanship / Creative
categories.description: Using practical and creative skills to build, make, and serve.

items.text: I have practical or creative skills I can use for God’s work.
I enjoy building, designing, decorating, making, or fixing things for ministry.
I can turn an idea into something real and useful.
I feel satisfied when I use my skills to serve others.
I have used my practical or creative skills to help a church project.
I have made something for the church that was useful or beautiful.
I love bringing ideas to life through my creativity.

categories.basis: Biblical practice of service
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Prayer in spiritual struggles
categories.description: Praying with people in spiritual difficulty, with mature church support.

items.text: I regularly pray for people facing spiritual struggles.
When someone describes a spiritual struggle, I listen carefully rather than assuming its cause.
I can remain calm and pray with someone who is frightened.
I am willing to pray with people who are struggling spiritually.
I have prayed with someone seeking freedom in Christ, with support from mature church leaders.

categories.basis: Biblical practice of service
categories.interpretationNote: Luke 10 describes Jesus’ disciples’ ministry and directs their joy toward salvation (verses 17–20). It does not list a separate deliverance gift. These prompts concern supported prayer, not diagnosing spiritual causes.

groups.title: Growing in character
groups.subtitle: Character that every believer is called to grow in
groups.intro: Faithfulness, humility, and attention to Scripture matter for every believer. Reflect on your present habits; these responses do not measure your spiritual worth or rank you against others.

categories.name: Faithfulness
categories.description: Being someone others can depend on, in small things and big things.

items.text: I can be trusted to finish what I am given to do.
I stay committed even when ministry gets hard.
I am willing to serve in small tasks before I get bigger ones.
I do not need praise to stay committed to ministry.
Others can depend on me to follow through on my commitments.
I take small responsibilities seriously.
I keep the promises I make to the church.
The church can count on me to show up and do what needs to be done.

categories.basis: Christian character and practice
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Humility & Teachability
categories.description: Staying humble and open to correction, especially in spiritual things.

items.text: I welcome others testing what I say against Scripture.
I acknowledge when I may be mistaken about a spiritual impression.
I avoid treating personal dislike or suspicion as spiritual discernment.
I am honest about uncertainty when sharing a spiritual impression.
I listen when mature believers correct me.
I serve with humility and under the leadership of the church.
I am willing to serve without receiving recognition.
I am willing to change my understanding when Scripture corrects it.

categories.basis: Christian character and practice
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.

categories.name: Rooted in Scripture
categories.description: Testing everything by the Bible and keeping spiritual things in good order.

items.text: I check spiritual impressions against the Bible.
I compare my spiritual impressions with Scripture rather than assuming they are from God.
I check messages presented as prophecy against Scripture.
I seek to follow Scripture’s instructions for orderly worship.
I check whether a spiritual message agrees with Scripture and builds up the church.
I turn to Scripture for guidance when praying with someone in spiritual difficulty.
I read Bible passages in context before applying them.
I am willing to set aside an idea when it conflicts with Scripture.

categories.basis: Christian character and practice
categories.interpretationNote: This is an area to reflect on through Scripture and service, not a measure of spiritual worth.
